confirmed_cause: RangeSource.block checks the shared 1800-second RangeSource lifetime before the next BGZF block. The same clock includes HTTP requests, synchronous boundary callbacks, line/record processing and guarded output writes. The label identifies the check site, not a measured zlib bottleneck.

metadata_only_batch_arithmetic.caveat: This is arithmetic on existing receipt offsets, not a network/decode benchmark. A real run may prefetch later planned windows and may still hit the original limits.

proposed_fix: Group at most eight consecutive missing 1 MB windows already declared by the unchanged TBI plan into one HTTP Range; retain them in a bounded 32 MB process-local compressed cache. Add phase timing without changing scientific transformations.
structural_costs: Each VCF compressed cache miss currently causes one serial 1,000,000-byte HTTP Range/open plus one actual root boundary callback.
309 distinct VCF windows were fetched; no duplicate-range requests or observed compressed-cache thrash occurred.
clean_record currently decodes and tab-splits all 3,331 source samples before processing the selected 20. This may contribute CPU/allocation cost, but no phase timings establish its share.
The four-window cache is sufficient for the observed forward stream. A larger cache is proposed only to hold batched prefetch, not as a demonstrated refetch cure.
unavailable_attribution: Request timestamps are recorded after the current before_request callback and before urlopen. Their gaps mix the previous HTTP transfer, decode/QC, writes and the next callback.
HTTP duration, guard callback duration, CPU time, decompressed bytes, candidate progress and last regional position were not retained in failed.json.
The largest 309.295322-second gap is consistent with several possible stalls and does not identify network, guard or parser as the sole bottleneck.
The full TBI region plan was not retained in the failure metadata and was not re-executed here. The remaining work and probability of finishing within 1800 seconds cannot be estimated reliably.
